**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Disallow memory tests from running on Windows** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1544
this is straightforward to fix, run the test suite with --nomemory, which is a SQLAlchemy flag that will deselect those tests.
also if you want to try out that patch, that also deselects those tests if you want to confirm

Patch set 1 helped, bringing the number of failures down from 22 to 13. Of those remaining, 9 are related to

> sqlite3.OperationalError: no such function: JSON_EXTRACT

Details here:

[py38_1544_PS1.txt](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/3772396/py38_1544_PS1.txt)

that would be because the pysqlite built into your windows python does not have the json extension installed, which is very strange because it is present in the linux version.   can you confirm the version of sqlite built into your python interpreter is 3.9 or greater 

```
Python 3.7.4 (default, Jul  9 2019, 16:32:37) 
[GCC 9.1.1 20190503 (Red Hat 9.1.1-1)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import sqlite3
>>> sqlite3.sqlite_version
'3.26.0'

```

```
Python 3.8.0 (tags/v3.8.0:fa919fd, Oct 14 2019, 19:37:50) [MSC v.1916 64 bit (AMD64)] on win32
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license()" for more information.
>>> import sqlite3
>>> sqlite3.sqlite_version
'3.28.0'
```

It seems that different platform builds of Python can include slightly different pieces, e.g., as discussed [here](https://github.com/microsoft/azure-pipelines-image-generation/issues/1083).
I'm happy to leave this closed, but please re-open if you'd like to pursue this further.
nope lets get the sqlite going

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Perform an active check for sqlite json extension** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1546
there's the next one to try

Okay, that eliminated the "no such function: JSON_EXTRACT" failures, so now we're down to 5:

[py38_1546_PS1.txt](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/3773281/py38_1546_PS1.txt)

can you try this, wild guess, otherwise I have to load windows and pdb

```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
index c45156d6b..60e29421c 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
@@ -1017,7 +1017,7 @@ class SuiteRequirements(Requirements):
         gc.collect() is called, as well as clean out unreferenced subclasses.
 
         """
-        return self.cpython
+        return self.cpython and not self._running_on_windows()
 
     @property
     def no_coverage(self):


```

Hit the limit of 25 errors:

> TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable

[patch1_out.txt](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/3773973/patch1_out.txt)

once more

```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
index c45156d6b..82f691f8a 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/requirements.py
@@ -1017,7 +1017,8 @@ class SuiteRequirements(Requirements):
         gc.collect() is called, as well as clean out unreferenced subclasses.
 
         """
-        return self.cpython
+
+        return self.cpython + self.no_windows
 
     @property
     def no_coverage(self):

```

Sorry, but I get the same 5 failures as in py38_1546_PS1.txt.

[patch2_out.txt](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/3774145/patch2_out.txt)

issue.title: session must close connection if begin fails
issue.body:
Hi,

I was constantly experiencing the following exception while using sqlalchemy + sqlite:
`SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread.`

Actually I don't think that I used the SA constructions in some wrong way, I always insured all transactions are either committed/rolled back and closed as well.

And long story short I found the reason (I was frequent reason for me at least ): If the `database is locked` exception occurs at the following [line](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/926952c4afe0b2e16c4a74f05958bded7b932760/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py#L441) then the underlying `Connection` and `_ConnectionFairy` object is dangled.

This in turn means that when `Session.close()` is called - the dangling `_ConnectionFairy`  is not released. And finally the noticed `_ConnectionFairy` object is often released in another thread and causes `SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread.` exception.

What should I do to handle this? I didn't find anything that could help in the SA docs.
Please don't tell me that sqlite is not for concurrency and so on, it's not precisely like that, it is probably not the best DB for concurrency but knowing all proc and cons of this simple DB I should be able to use this.

And also, why didn't you store the connection (which is coded [here](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/926952c4afe0b2e16c4a74f05958bded7b932760/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py#L443)) before beginning the transaction? It would solve the issue forever.

Thank you.
